chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the shot game whose owner finds it the next morning. Can he eat from it? So he said: If he knows that it was his shot which killed it, then let him eat from that, when he had already invoked the name (of Allah).

key_terms.الرَّمِيَّة: Shot game/prey — an animal that has been struck by a projectile weapon such as an arrow
key_terms.سَمَّى: Named (Allah) — i.e., said Bismillah (In the name of God) at the time of shooting, a required condition for halal hunting

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat game found dead the next morning if shot by arrow in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a common jurisprudential question in Islamic hunting law: if a hunter shoots an animal with an arrow but only finds it dead the next day, is the meat permissible to eat? Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes two conditions for permissibility: (1) the hunter must be certain that his arrow was what killed the animal — not another cause — and (2) he must have said Bismillah at the time of shooting. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that the intention and invocation at the moment of hunting are determinative, even when the hunter discovers the animal later.
